- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast shows strong upward bias, apply downward correction of 3–5% to prevent false rallies.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model tends to overcorrect; reduce subsequent forecast values by 2–4% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.30–0.67) and forecast is trending, apply a 1–3% downward bias to account for lagged market adjustment.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by 2–3% over 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period to reflect diminishing momentum.
- For sentiment history with repeated low values (0.00–0.20), model tends to overestimate recovery; apply 2–4% downward adjustment to avoid false optimism.
